data.name: Avvesh
data.gender_notes: Avvesh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Avvesh is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Av-Vesha', meaning 'God's Grace'. This name is given to a child born under the divine blessings of the gods, symbolizing their presence and protection throughout the child's life. The name Avvesh carries the meaning “God's Grace” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Avvesh usually hope their child will grow to embody god's grace and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Avvesh belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God's Grace.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Avvesh total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

historical_references.reference: Avvesh, also known as Avvaiyyar, was a renowned Tamil poetess who lived during the Sangam period (approximately 200 BC to 500 AD). She was a patron of the arts and a great devotee of Lord Shiva. Her works include poems on love, beauty, wisdom, and the power of the goddesses.
historical_references.context: Renowned Tamil poetess, devotee of Lord Shiva

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Avvesh can be found in the Puranic literature, particularly in the Skanda Purana. In this text, Avvesh is mentioned as a great sage who was blessed by Lord Shiva to have the ability to cure all diseases. He is also known for his devotion to Lord Murugan (Lord Subrahmanya), and is believed to have received the divine powers to heal through the grace of the god.
historical_references.context: Great sage, healer, devotee of Lord Murugan
